package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a double-free vulnerability (CVE-2019-11932) in its native GIF parsing code, which can be exploited by attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause denial of service on devices using the library. The vulnerability is triggered by specially crafted GIF files, making any application using the vulnerable versions susceptible to remote exploitation.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a GIF image is parsed by the application)
execution_context.file_location: native code (decoding.c, specifically in the DDGifSlurp function)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This code attempts to free the same memory region twice if a zero-sized image is encountered, leading to a double-free vulnerability.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Double-free vulnerabilities are a well-known class of memory corruption bugs that can be exploited to achieve arbitrary code execution or denial of service. The code does not properly check if the memory has already been freed before attempting to free it again.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal image parsing code should ensure that memory is only freed once and should validate input files to prevent malformed or malicious files from triggering unsafe memory operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code may free memory in error handling, but should always guard against double-free by nullifying pointers or using safe memory management patterns.
key_indicators: free() called twice on the same pointer
lack of input validation for zero-sized images
vulnerability triggered by crafted input files

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious GIF file with a zero-sized image segment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious file is delivered to the victim (e.g., via WhatsApp or any app using the vulnerable library).

attack_chain.action: Victim opens or previews the malicious GIF file in an affected application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Application invokes the vulnerable GIF parsing code.

attack_chain.action: The DDGifSlurp function in decoding.c processes the GIF, encounters the zero-sized image, and executes the double-free code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Memory corruption occurs, potentially allowing arbitrary code execution or denial of service.

attack_chain.action: Attacker's payload (if present in the crafted file) may execute with the privileges of the application.

behavioral_signatures: Application crashes or exhibits undefined behavior after opening certain GIF files
Unexpected memory corruption or double-free errors in native code
Abnormal process termination when parsing media files
file_indicators: GIF files with zero-sized image segments
Malformed or unusually small GIF files delivered via messaging or file transfer
network_indicators: Delivery of suspicious GIF files via messaging platforms (e.g., WhatsApp, chat apps)
No direct network indicators from the vulnerability itself, but may be correlated with delivery of crafted files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs and crash reports for double-free or memory corruption errors in native GIF parsing code. Use static analysis to identify vulnerable versions of the pl.droidsonroids.gif:android-gif-drawable library. Scan incoming GIF files for zero-sized image segments or malformed structures. Alert on delivery or opening of suspicious GIF files in applications using the affected library versions.
